source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר דָּוִד֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֖י הַשִּׁירָ֣ה הַזֹּ֑את בְּיוֹם֩ הִצִּ֨יל יְהוָ֥ה אֹת֛וֹ מִכַּ֥ף כָּל־אֹיְבָ֖יו וּמִכַּ֥ף שָׁאֽוּל׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke David to YHWH the words of this song on [the] day YHWH delivered him from [the] palm of all his enemies and from [the] palm of Saul.

en.L: And David spoke to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the words of this song on the day [when] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} delivered him from the palm of all his enemies and from the palm of Saul.
en.B: David sang the words of this song to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rescued him from the power of all his enemies and from the power of Saul.
en.R: David sang this song to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saved him from all his enemies, and from Saul.

decisions.reason: This song is also found, with small differences, as Psalm 18. Its wording here follows Psalm 18 wherever the Hebrew is the same, and each verse names where the two differ. Here, near the end of David's story, it looks back over all his wars (chapters 5, 8, 10 and 21), before his last words in 23:1-7.

Psalm 18:1 is a title: "For the director. Of the servant of the LORD, of David, who spoke ...". Here the narrator says "And David spoke". The psalm also has "from the hand of Saul" where this verse repeats "from the palm".

decisions.choice: the palm of all his enemies: their power
decisions.reason: The palm and the hand stand for power and control.

decisions.choice: and from Saul: the enemy of David's early years
decisions.reason: Saul hunted David for years (1 Samuel 18-26). He is named apart from the other enemies because he was Israel's king and the LORD's anointed, whom David would not harm (1 Samuel 24:7).
The verb means to speak, but what David spoke was a song; Balanced and Readable say "sang", as at Psalm 18:1.

source.text: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר יְהוָ֛ה סַֽלְעִ֥י וּמְצֻדָתִ֖י וּמְפַלְטִי־לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, YHWH [is] my rock and my stronghold and my deliverer for me,

en.L: And he said: \q "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] my crag and my stronghold and my deliverer for me,
en.B: He said: \q "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is my cliff, my stronghold, the one who sets me free,
en.R: He said: \q "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is like a high rock where I am safe. He is like a fort, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rescues me.

decisions.reason: The whole song, to verse 51, is David's speech; the quotation opens here and closes at the end of the chapter. Verses 2 and 3 are one long sentence of names for God.

decisions.choice: rock, stronghold: places of safety in the hills
decisions.reason: David hid from Saul in the rocky heights and strongholds of the wilderness (1 Samuel 23:14, 25). The words for these places (sela', metsudah, and misgav in verse 3) become names for God himself.
Psalm 18:2 has one more line after "And he said": "I love you, LORD, my strength." Psalm 18:3 has no "for me" after "my deliverer".

decisions.choice: my deliverer for me: my own deliverer
decisions.reason: The added "for me" stresses that the LORD is David's own rescuer.
Balanced and Readable carry the stress of "for me" with "my" and "me" rather than repeat it.

decisions.choice: like a high rock, like a fort
decisions.reason: Readable makes the pictures comparisons, as at Psalm 18:3, so that young readers do not take them literally.

source.text: אֱלֹהֵ֥י צוּרִ֖י אֶחֱסֶה־בּ֑וֹ מָגִנִּ֞י וְקֶ֣רֶן יִשְׁעִ֗י מִשְׂגַּבִּי֙ וּמְנוּסִ֔י מֹשִׁעִ֕י מֵחָמָ֖ס תֹּשִׁעֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: God of my rock, I take refuge in him, my shield and [the] horn of my salvation, my high refuge and my place of escape, my savior; from violence you save me.

en.L: the God of my rock in whom I take refuge, \q my shield and the horn of my salvation, my high refuge and my place of escape, \q my savior; from violence {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} save me.
en.B: my God, my rock, in whom I shelter, \q my shield, my strong salvation, my tower on the heights and my place of escape, \q my savior; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} save me from violence.
en.R: My God is like a rock where I can run for safety. \q He protects me like a shield. He is strong to save me. He is like a tower high above my enemies, a place where I can escape. \q He is the one who saves me. You save me from people who do violence.

decisions.choice: the God of my rock: my God, who is my rock
decisions.reason: The phrase joins God and rock: the God who is David's rock. The song ends with the same kind of phrase, "the God of the rock of my salvation" (verse 47).

decisions.choice: the horn of my salvation: my strong savior
decisions.reason: A horn is the strength of an animal and so a picture of power (Psalm 75:11; 1 Samuel 2:1); "the horn of my salvation" is the power that saves me.

decisions.choice: you save me: the song speaks to God
decisions.reason: After the list of names the song turns for a moment from speaking of God to speaking to him, as it does again in verses 29 and 49.

Psalm 18:3 has "my God, my rock" where this verse has "the God of my rock", and it ends at "my high refuge". The last words here, "and my place of escape, my savior; from violence you save me", are not in the psalm.

decisions.choice: my strong salvation (B); He is strong to save me (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the horn means (m2), as at Psalm 18:3.
Balanced gives the sense of "the God of my rock" (m1) in the words of Psalm 18:3.

decisions.choice: like a rock, like a shield, like a tower
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, Readable makes the pictures comparisons.

source.text: מְהֻלָּ֖ל אֶקְרָ֣א יְהוָ֑ה וּמֵאֹיְבַ֖י אִוָּשֵֽׁעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The one who is] to be praised I call [on], YHWH, and from my enemies I am saved.

en.L: [The one who is] worthy of praise I call [on], {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and from my enemies I am saved.
en.B: I call on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who is worthy of praise, \q and from my enemies I am rescued.
en.R: I call to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who deserves all praise, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saves me from my enemies.

decisions.choice: I call, I am saved: what always happens
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the unfinished form: whenever David calls, he is saved. Verses 5-20 then tell one great rescue.

decisions.choice: the one to be praised: worthy of praise
decisions.reason: The word (mehullal) means praised, deserving praise (Psalm 48:2; 96:4).
Psalm 18:4 has the same words, with a longer spelling of "from".

source.text: כִּ֥י אֲפָפֻ֖נִי מִשְׁבְּרֵי־מָ֑וֶת נַחֲלֵ֥י בְלִיַּ֖עַל יְבַעֲתֻֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: For encompassed me [the] breakers of death; torrents of worthlessness terrified me.

en.L: For the breakers of death encompassed me; \q torrents of destruction terrified me.
en.B: For the waves of death swirled around me; \q floods of ruin overwhelmed me with terror.
en.R: Death was like waves crashing all around me. \q Danger poured over me like a flood, and I was terrified.

decisions.choice: breakers: waves that break over a person
decisions.reason: The word (mishbar) is a breaking wave (Psalm 42:8; Jonah 2:4). With the torrents of the next line, death is pictured as a flood.
The word (beliyya'al) means what is worthless and destructive; it later became a name for evil and for Satan (2 Corinthians 6:15).
The verse begins to explain the danger from which he called to the LORD (verse 4).

Psalm 18:5 has "the cords of death" (chevel), matching verse 6, where this verse has "the breakers of death", matching the flood of the next line. The psalm has no "for" at the start, and joins the lines with "and".
Readable lets the link to verse 4 be understood, to keep the sentence short.

source.text: חֶבְלֵ֥י שְׁא֖וֹל סַבֻּ֑נִי קִדְּמֻ֖נִי מֹֽקְשֵׁי־מָֽוֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] cords of Sheol surrounded me; confronted me [the] snares of death.

en.L: The cords of Sheol surrounded me; \q the snares of death confronted me.
en.B: The ropes of Sheol coiled around me; \q death's traps lay right in front of me.
en.R: It was as if the place of the dead had me tied up. \q Death had set traps for me, and I could not get away.

decisions.choice: Sheol: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: Sheol is the place of the dead, pictured under the earth (1 Samuel 2:6). Here it is a hunter that has David bound.

decisions.choice: the snares of death confronted me: death stood in my way
decisions.reason: Death is a hunter whose traps meet the singer at every turn (Psalm 116:3).
Psalm 18:6 has the same words, with small differences of spelling.
Readable explains the name, as at Psalm 18:6.

source.text: בַּצַּר־לִי֙ אֶקְרָ֣א יְהוָ֔ה וְאֶל־אֱלֹהַ֖י אֶקְרָ֑א וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע מֵהֵֽיכָלוֹ֙ קוֹלִ֔י וְשַׁוְעָתִ֖י בְּאָזְנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: In my distress I called [on] YHWH, and to my God I called; and he heard from his temple my voice, and my cry for help [was] in his ears.

en.L: In my distress I called [on] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and to my God I called; \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heard my voice from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple, and my cry [came] into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ears.
en.B: When I was hard pressed I called on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; I called to my God. \q Out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} listened to my voice; my cry reached {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ears.
en.R: When I was in trouble, I called out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I called to my God. \q He was in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heard me. My cry reached {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ears.

decisions.choice: his temple: God's dwelling in heaven
decisions.reason: As in Psalm 11:4, the temple is God's palace in heaven, from which he comes down in verses 8-17.

decisions.choice: I called, he heard: the story of the rescue
decisions.reason: Here the song turns to tell the rescue as a past event.
Psalm 18:7 has "I cried for help" (shava') in place of the second "I called", "he heard" without "and", and "my cry before him came into his ears" where this verse has "my cry into his ears".

source.text: וַיִּתְגָּעַ֤שׁוַתִּרְעַשׁ֙ הָאָ֔רֶץ מוֹסְד֥וֹת הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם יִרְגָּ֑זוּ וַיִּֽתְגָּעֲשׁ֖וּ כִּֽי־חָ֥רָה לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And shook and quaked the earth; [the] foundations of the heavens trembled and shook, for it burned to him.

en.L: And the earth shook and quaked; \q the foundations of the heavens trembled and shook, \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was angry.
en.B: Then the earth shuddered and rocked; \q the foundations of the heavens trembled and were shaken, \q because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was furious.
en.R: Then the earth shook. \q Even the pillars that hold up the sky shook, \q because God was very angry.

decisions.choice: the earth shook: the LORD comes as at Sinai
decisions.reason: Verses 8-16 picture the LORD coming down in storm and earthquake, as he did at Mount Sinai (Exodus 19:16-18) and when he led Israel out of Egypt (Judges 5:4-5; Psalm 68:8-9).

decisions.choice: the foundations of the heavens: the mountains that hold up the sky
decisions.reason: The sky was pictured as resting on pillars at the ends of the earth (Job 26:11). The whole world, from the sky down to its base, shakes when God comes.

decisions.choice: it burned to him: he was angry
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "it burned to him", a common way of saying that anger flared up (Genesis 4:5).

Psalm 18:8 has "the foundations of the mountains" where this verse has "the foundations of the heavens". The first verb is written here as in the psalm but marked to be read in another form of the same verb, with the same sense.

decisions.choice: God; the pillars that hold up the sky
decisions.reason: Readable names who was angry, and says what the foundations of the heavens are (m2).

source.text: עָלָ֤ה עָשָׁן֙ בְּאַפּ֔וֹ וְאֵ֥שׁ מִפִּ֖יו תֹּאכֵ֑ל גֶּחָלִ֖ים בָּעֲר֥וּ מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Went up smoke in his nose, and fire from his mouth devoured; coals burned from it.

en.L: Smoke went up from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} nostrils, \q and fire from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth devoured; \q coals blazed from it.
en.B: Smoke rose from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} nostrils, \q and fire that consumes came from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth; \q burning coals flamed out of it.
en.R: Smoke came out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} nose. \q Fire that burns up everything came out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth, with red-hot coals.

decisions.choice: smoke in his nose: a picture of anger
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the nose is the seat of anger (the word 'af means both); the snorting of fury is pictured as smoke and fire.

decisions.choice: fire from his mouth: God's holy anger
decisions.reason: The LORD is a consuming fire (Deuteronomy 4:24). The picture is poetry for God's power against those who oppose him.
Psalm 18:9 has the same words.

source.text: וַיֵּ֥ט שָׁמַ֖יִם וַיֵּרַ֑ד וַעֲרָפֶ֖ל תַּ֥חַת רַגְלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he bent [the] heavens and came down, and thick darkness [was] under his feet.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} bent the heavens and came down, \q and thick darkness [was] under {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet.
en.B: He bowed the heavens low and came down; \q storm clouds were dark beneath {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet.
en.R: He opened the sky and came down. \q Dark clouds were under {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet.

decisions.choice: bent the heavens: bowed the sky down
decisions.reason: The verb (natah) means to stretch out or bend; the sky bows down as God comes (Psalm 144:5).

decisions.choice: thick darkness: the dark cloud around God
decisions.reason: The thick darkness ('arafel) is the cloud in which God came to Sinai (Exodus 20:21; Deuteronomy 4:11).
Psalm 18:10 has the same words.

source.text: וַיִּרְכַּ֥ב עַל־כְּר֖וּב וַיָּעֹ֑ף וַיֵּרָ֖א עַל־כַּנְפֵי־רֽוּחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he rode on a cherub and flew, and he was seen on [the] wings of [the] wind.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rode on a cherub and flew, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was seen on the wings of the wind.
en.B: Riding on a cherub, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} flew; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} appeared on the wings of the wind.
en.R: He flew, riding on a cherub. \q He was seen, carried by the wind.

decisions.choice: a cherub: a winged being who serves God
decisions.reason: Cherubim guard God's presence (Genesis 3:24) and carry his throne (Ezekiel 10); the LORD is "enthroned on the cherubim" (1 Samuel 4:4; 2 Samuel 6:2). Here a cherub is his chariot.

decisions.choice: he was seen: God's coming made visible
decisions.reason: The God who comes hidden in cloud (verses 10, 12) is still seen in the storm as it rushes on the wind.
Psalm 18:11 has "and he swooped" (da'ah) where this verse has "and he was seen" (ra'ah). In Hebrew writing the two words differ by one letter, d for r, and the two letters look much alike.

source.text: וַיָּ֥שֶׁת חֹ֛שֶׁךְ סְבִיבֹתָ֖יו סֻכּ֑וֹת חַֽשְׁרַת־מַ֖יִם עָבֵ֥י שְׁחָקִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he set darkness around him [as] shelters, a mass of waters, clouds of skies.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set darkness around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [as] shelters, \q a mass of waters, clouds of the skies.
en.B: He made darkness a tent all around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q a mass of rain clouds, thick clouds of the sky.
en.R: He put darkness all around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} like a tent. \q He was covered with heavy rain clouds.

decisions.reason: The word (sukkah) is a shelter or booth; the storm clouds are God's tent (Job 36:29).

decisions.choice: a mass of waters: heavy rain clouds
decisions.reason: The word (chasherah) is found only here. A related word names the hubs of a wheel, where the spokes come together (1 Kings 7:33), so it probably means a gathering of water: clouds heavy with rain.

Psalm 18:12 has "his hiding place" and "his canopy" where this verse has "shelters", and "darkness of waters" (cheshkat) where this verse has "a mass of waters" (chasherat), a word that differs by one letter. The psalm has no "and" at the start.
The plural "shelters" is one covering all around God; Balanced and Readable say "a tent".

source.text: מִנֹּ֖גַהּ נֶגְדּ֑וֹ בָּעֲר֖וּ גַּחֲלֵי־אֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: From [the] brightness before him burned coals of fire.

en.L: From the brightness before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} \q coals of fire blazed.
en.B: Out of the brightness in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} \q burning coals flamed up.
en.R: From the bright light around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} \q burning coals blazed out.

decisions.reason: The brightness (nogah) is the blazing light of God's presence (Ezekiel 1:4, 28).
The burning coals that flash out of the storm are lightning (Psalm 140:11 uses the same picture).
Psalm 18:13 has "his clouds passed through, hail and coals of fire"; this verse has "coals of fire burned", with the verb of verse 9, and no hail.

source.text: יַרְעֵ֥ם מִן־שָׁמַ֖יִם יְהוָ֑ה וְעֶלְי֖וֹן יִתֵּ֥ן קוֹלֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Thundered from heaven YHWH, and [the] Most High gave his voice.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} thundered from the heavens, \q and the Most High gave forth {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} thundered from heaven; \q the Most High raised {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} thundered from the sky. \q The God who is above all spoke with a voice like thunder.

decisions.reason: God's voice is the thunder (Psalm 29:3-9).

decisions.choice: the Most High: God above all
decisions.reason: The title ('Elyon) names God as higher than every power in heaven and on earth (Genesis 14:18-20; Psalm 7:18).
Psalm 18:14 begins with "and", has "in the heavens" where this verse has "from heaven", and ends with "hail and coals of fire", words this verse does not have.

decisions.choice: The God who is above all
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title, as at Psalm 18:14.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח חִצִּ֖ים וַיְפִיצֵ֑ם בָּרָ֖ק וַיָּהֹֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he sent arrows and scattered them, lightning, and routed [them].

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent out arrows and scattered them, \q lightning, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} routed [them].
en.B: He let arrows fly and scattered the enemy; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent lightning and threw them into confusion.
en.R: He shot arrows and made the enemy run away. \q He sent lightning, and they did not know where to go.

decisions.reason: The lightning bolts are God's arrows (Psalm 77:18; Habakkuk 3:11).

decisions.choice: lightning: a second thing he sent out
decisions.reason: The line is short: "lightning, and he routed". Lightning is the second weapon God sends, after the arrows.
The verb (hamam) is used of God throwing an army into confusion (Exodus 14:24; Joshua 10:10).

Psalm 18:15 has "his arrows" and "lightnings he shot" (rav); this verse has "arrows" and "lightning", without the verb. The last verb is written as in the psalm, "and he routed them", and marked to be read "and he routed", with the same sense.
"Them" are David's enemies, and the lightning is sent like the arrows; Balanced and Readable say so.

source.text: וַיֵּֽרָאוּ֙ אֲפִ֣קֵי יָ֔ם יִגָּל֖וּ מֹסְד֣וֹת תֵּבֵ֑ל בְּגַעֲרַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה מִנִּשְׁמַ֖ת ר֥וּחַ אַפּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And were seen [the] channels of [the] sea; were uncovered [the] foundations of [the] world at [the] rebuke of YHWH, at [the] blast of [the] breath of his nose.

en.L: And the channels of the sea appeared; \q the foundations of the world were laid bare \q at the rebuke of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q at the blast of the breath of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} nostrils.
en.B: The beds of the sea came into view; \q the world's foundations lay bare \q at the rebuke of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q at the blast of breath from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} nostrils.
en.R: The bottom of the sea could be seen. \q The deep roots of the earth were uncovered \q when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shouted in anger and breathed out hard.

decisions.choice: the blast of his nostrils: as at the Red Sea
decisions.reason: At the sea "by the blast of your nostrils the waters piled up" (Exodus 15:8), and the seabed was laid bare. The rescue of David is told like the rescue at the sea.
God's rebuke (ge'arah) drives back the waters (Psalm 104:7).

Psalm 18:16 has "channels of water" where this verse has "channels of the sea". It speaks to God, "at your rebuke, LORD ... of your nostrils", where this verse speaks of him, "at the rebuke of the LORD ... of his nostrils".

decisions.choice: shouted in anger and breathed out hard
decisions.reason: Readable says what the rebuke and the blast of breath are, as at Psalm 18:16.

source.text: יִשְׁלַ֥ח מִמָּר֖וֹם יִקָּחֵ֑נִי יַֽמְשֵׁ֖נִי מִמַּ֥יִם רַבִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: He sent from on high, he took me; he drew me out of many waters.

en.L: He reached down from on high, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took me; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} drew me out of many waters.
en.B: From on high {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stretched out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and seized me; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} pulled me out of deep waters.
en.R: He reached down from heaven and grabbed me. \q He pulled me out of the deep water.

decisions.choice: drew me out: the verb of Moses' name
decisions.reason: The verb (mashah) is found only here, in Psalm 18:17 and in Exodus 2:10, where Pharaoh's daughter names Moses because she "drew him out" of the water.

decisions.choice: many waters: the floods of death and danger
decisions.reason: The waters of verse 5; many waters are the forces of chaos and death (Psalm 32:6; 144:7).

decisions.choice: he sent: he reached out his hand
decisions.reason: "He sent" is short for "he sent out his hand" (Psalm 144:7).
Psalm 18:17 has the same words.

source.text: יַצִּילֵ֕נִי מֵאֹיְבִ֖י עָ֑ז מִשֹּׂ֣נְאַ֔י כִּ֥י אָמְצ֖וּ מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: He rescued me from my enemy, strong, from those who hated me, for they were stronger than I.

en.L: He rescued me from my strong enemy, \q from those who hated me, \q for they were too strong for me.
en.B: He snatched me away from my powerful enemy, \q from those who hated me, \q because they were stronger than I was.
en.R: He saved me from my powerful enemy and from all who hated me. \q They were too strong for me to fight.

decisions.choice: my strong enemy: one enemy above all
decisions.reason: The singular "enemy" may be Saul (verse 1) or every enemy taken together.

decisions.choice: they were too strong for me: rescue by God alone
decisions.reason: David does not boast of his own strength; the rescue is God's work.
Psalm 18:18 has "and from those who hated me"; this verse has no "and". The sense is the same.

source.text: יְקַדְּמֻ֖נִי בְּי֣וֹם אֵידִ֑י וַיְהִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה מִשְׁעָ֖ן לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: They confronted me in [the] day of my calamity, but YHWH was a support to me.

en.L: They confronted me in the day of my calamity, \q but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was a support to me.
en.B: They came at me on my day of disaster, \q but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} held me up.
en.R: They attacked me when I was in deep trouble. \q But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} took care of me.

decisions.reason: The word ('ed) is a crushing disaster (Proverbs 1:26-27).

decisions.choice: support: a staff to lean on
decisions.reason: The word (mish'an) is something to lean on, like a staff (Psalm 23:4 uses a related word).
Psalm 18:19 has "became a support" (with "for"); this verse has "was a support". The sense is the same.

source.text: וַיֹּצֵ֥א לַמֶּרְחָ֖ב אֹתִ֑י יְחַלְּצֵ֖נִי כִּי־חָ֥פֵֽץ בִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he brought out to the broad place me; he rescued me, for he delighted in me.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought me out into the broad place; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rescued me, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} delighted in me.
en.B: He led me out into open country; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set me free, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was pleased with me.
en.R: He brought me out to a safe, open place. \q He saved me because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was happy with me.

decisions.choice: the broad place: freedom and safety
decisions.reason: Trouble in Hebrew is a narrow place where one is hemmed in; rescue is room to move (Psalm 4:2; 118:5).

decisions.choice: he delighted in me: he was pleased with me
decisions.reason: The verb (chafets) is used of God's pleasure in a person (Psalm 22:9). David used it of himself when he fled from Absalom: "if he says, 'I have no pleasure in you'" (15:26).
Psalm 18:20 joins "me" to the verb "brought out"; here it stands as a separate word after "the broad place". The sense is the same.

source.text: יִגְמְלֵ֥נִי יְהוָ֖ה כְּצִדְקָתִ֑י כְּבֹ֥ר יָדַ֖י יָשִׁ֥יב לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: YHWH dealt with me according to my righteousness; according to [the] cleanness of my hands he repaid me.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} dealt with me according to my righteousness; \q according to the cleanness of my hands {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} repaid me.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} treated me as my right conduct deserved; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rewarded me because my hands were clean.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was good to me because I did what was right. \q I had not done wrong, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} blessed me.

decisions.choice: according to my righteousness: loyalty, not sinlessness
decisions.reason: David is not claiming that he never sinned; this book has told of his sin with Bathsheba (chapters 11-12). He means that he stayed loyal to the LORD and did not take matters into his own hands; he twice spared Saul's life (1 Samuel 24 and 26). The same words close this section in verse 25.

decisions.choice: cleanness of my hands: innocence in what I have done
decisions.reason: Clean hands are hands that have done no wrong (Psalm 24:4).
The verb (gamal) means to deal with someone, to give back what is due (Psalm 13:6).
Psalm 18:21 uses another form of the word for righteousness (tsedeq, here tsedaqah). The sense is the same.

source.text: כִּ֥י שָׁמַ֖רְתִּי דַּרְכֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹ֥א רָשַׁ֖עְתִּי מֵאֱלֹהָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For I have kept [the] ways of YHWH and have not acted wickedly from my God.

en.L: For I have kept the ways of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and I have not acted wickedly [to depart] from my God.
en.B: For I have walked in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s ways \q and have not turned from my God to do evil.
en.R: I have obeyed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q I have not turned away from my God to do evil.

decisions.choice: acted wickedly from my God: left God to do wrong
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins "act wickedly" and "from": to sin by leaving God.

decisions.choice: kept the ways of the LORD: lived as he commands
decisions.reason: The LORD's ways are the life he has commanded (Deuteronomy 8:6).
Psalm 18:22 has the same words.

source.text: כִּ֥י כָל־מִשְׁפָּטָ֖יו לְנֶגְדִּ֑י וְחֻקֹּתָ֖יו לֹא־אָס֥וּר מִמֶּֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: For all his judgments [are] before me, and his statutes, I do not turn aside from it.

en.L: For all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} judgments [are] before me, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes, I have not turned aside from them.
en.B: All {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rulings have been in front of me; \q I have not turned aside from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws.
en.R: I keep all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws in mind. \q I have not stopped obeying {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rules.

decisions.reason: Two common words for God's law (Deuteronomy 4:1, 8).
To keep the law before one's eyes is to live by it (Psalm 16:8).

decisions.choice: from it: from his statutes taken together
decisions.reason: "It" is singular: the statutes are taken as one whole.
Psalm 18:23 has "I have not put away from me" (asir, I cause to turn aside); this verse has "I have not turned aside from it" (asur).
Balanced and Readable use everyday words for the statutes, as at Psalm 18:23.

source.text: וָאֶהְיֶ֥ה תָמִ֖ים ל֑וֹ וָאֶשְׁתַּמְּרָ֖ה מֵעֲוֺנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I was blameless to him, and I kept myself from my iniquity.

en.L: And I was blameless toward {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and I kept myself from my iniquity.
en.B: I was whole-hearted toward {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q I guarded myself from sin.
en.R: I was loyal to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all my heart. \q I kept myself from doing wrong.

decisions.reason: The word (tamim) means whole and sound; of a person, one whose life is all of a piece in loyalty to God (Genesis 17:1; Psalm 15:2).
"My iniquity" is the sin he might have committed; he kept himself from it.
Psalm 18:24 has "with him" ('immo) where this verse has "to him" (lo). The two verbs are written in slightly longer forms here, with the same sense.

source.text: וַיָּ֧שֶׁב יְהוָ֛ה לִ֖י כְּצִדְקָתִ֑י כְּבֹרִ֖י לְנֶ֥גֶד עֵינָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And YHWH repaid me according to my righteousness, according to my cleanness before his eyes.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has repaid me according to my righteousness, \q according to my cleanness before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes.
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rewarded me for doing right, \q for the cleanness {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could see in me.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rewarded me because I did what was right. \q He saw that I had not done wrong.

decisions.choice: repaid me according to my righteousness: verse 21 again
decisions.reason: The words of verse 21 return, closing this part of the song.

decisions.choice: before his eyes: as God sees it
decisions.reason: The cleanness is what God himself sees, not only what others see.
Psalm 18:25 has "the cleanness of my hands", as in verse 21, where this verse has "my cleanness". The word for righteousness differs in form, as in verse 21.

source.text: עִם־חָסִ֖יד תִּתְחַסָּ֑ד עִם־גִּבּ֥וֹר תָּמִ֖ים תִּתַּמָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: With [the] loyal you show yourself loyal; with [the] blameless mighty man you show yourself blameless.

en.L: With the loyal {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} show {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} loyal; \q with the blameless mighty {{gender:one|man}} {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} show {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} blameless.
en.B: To the faithful {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are faithful; \q to the strong who have integrity {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} show integrity.
en.R: You keep faith with people who keep faith with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q You are good to strong people who live good lives.

decisions.choice: you show yourself loyal: God answers people as they are
decisions.reason: Verses 26-27 state the rule behind verses 21-25: God deals with each person in keeping with how that person lives toward him.

decisions.choice: the loyal: one who keeps faith
decisions.reason: The word (chasid) is related to chesed, faithful love: one who keeps faith with God (Psalm 4:4; 16:10).

decisions.choice: the mighty man: anyone strong who lives this way
decisions.reason: The word (gibbor) is a strong man or warrior. The line is not about warriors only: it means anyone who lives with integrity.
Psalm 18:26 has "man" (gever) where this verse has "mighty man" (gibbor), a word from the same root.
The word means a strong man, but here anyone who lives this way (m3).

source.text: עִם־נָבָ֖ר תִּתָּבָ֑ר וְעִם־עִקֵּ֖שׁ תִּתַּפָּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: With [the one who] purifies himself you show yourself pure, but with [the] crooked you show yourself twisted.

en.L: With the pure {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} show {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} pure, \q but with the crooked {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} show {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} shrewd.
en.B: To the pure {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} prove {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} pure, \q but with the crooked {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are subtle.
en.R: You are pure with people who are pure. \q But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are clever with people who are twisted and false.

decisions.choice: with the crooked you are shrewd: God outwits them
decisions.reason: The verb (patal, to twist) is a different word from "crooked" ('iqqesh). God does not become crooked; he matches the schemes of the crooked and turns them back on them (Proverbs 3:34).

decisions.choice: the pure: one who keeps himself clean
decisions.reason: The form means one who purifies himself, keeping his life clean.
Psalm 18:27 writes both verbs in fuller forms (titbarar, titpattal); here they are shorter. The sense is the same.

source.text: וְאֶת־עַ֥ם עָנִ֖י תּוֹשִׁ֑יעַ וְעֵינֶ֖יךָ עַל־רָמִ֥ים תַּשְׁפִּֽיל׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] afflicted people you save, and your eyes [are] on [the] haughty; you bring [them] low.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} save an afflicted people, \q but {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes [are] on the haughty; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bring [them] low.
en.B: You rescue people who are humbled, \q but {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes are on the proud, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bring them down.
en.R: You save people who are poor and humble. \q But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} watch the proud, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bring them down.

decisions.reason: The word ('ani) means poor and pressed down, and so dependent on God (Psalm 9:13).

decisions.choice: your eyes are on the haughty: God watches them to humble them
decisions.reason: God's eyes are on the proud as a judge's are, and he brings them down (Isaiah 2:11-12).
Psalm 18:28 has "For you save an afflicted people, but haughty eyes you bring low". Here the verse begins with "and", and the eyes are God's: "your eyes are on the haughty".

source.text: כִּֽי־אַתָּ֥ה נֵירִ֖י יְהוָ֑ה וַיהוָ֖ה יַגִּ֥יהַּ חָשְׁכִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For you [are] my lamp, YHWH, and YHWH makes bright my darkness.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] my lamp, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} makes my darkness bright.
en.B: You are my lamp, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brightens my darkness.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are like a lamp for me. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} makes my dark times bright.

decisions.choice: my lamp: the light of my life
decisions.reason: A burning lamp is a picture of life and hope; the lamp of the wicked goes out (Job 18:6). In 21:17 David's men call him "the lamp of Israel"; here David calls the LORD his own lamp.

decisions.choice: you ... the LORD: the song moves between "you" and "he"
decisions.reason: The line speaks to God and then of him, as songs of praise often do.
Psalm 18:29 has "you light my lamp, LORD; my God makes my darkness bright". Here the LORD is himself the lamp, and "the LORD" is repeated where the psalm has "my God".
Readable makes the picture a comparison.

source.text: כִּ֥י בְכָ֖ה אָר֣וּץ גְּד֑וּד בֵּאלֹהַ֖י אֲדַלֶּג־שֽׁוּר׃

records.literal_gloss: For by you I run [against] a troop; by my God I leap over a wall.

en.L: For by {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I run [against] a troop; \q by my God I leap over a wall.
en.B: With {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I can rush an armed band; \q by the strength of my God I can vault a wall.
en.R: With {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} help I can attack a whole army. \q With God's help I can jump over a city wall.

decisions.reason: The word (gedud) is a band of raiders (1 Samuel 30:8). The verb may mean "run" or, read slightly differently, "crush".

decisions.choice: leap over a wall: storm a city
decisions.reason: A wall is a city wall; with God's help David takes walled cities (5:6-7).
Psalm 18:30 has "and by my God"; this verse has no "and". The sense is the same.
Readable says that "by you" means by God's help.

source.text: הָאֵ֖ל תָּמִ֣ים דַּרְכּ֑וֹ אִמְרַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ צְרוּפָ֔ה מָגֵ֣ן ה֔וּא לְכֹ֖ל הַחֹסִ֥ים בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: The God, blameless [is] his way; [the] word of YHWH [is] refined; a shield he [is] to all who take refuge in him.

en.L: [As for] God, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way [is] blameless; \q the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] refined; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] a shield to all who take refuge in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: This is God: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way is without flaw; \q the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is tested and true; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is a shield for all who make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} their refuge.
en.R: God always does what is right. \q What {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says is always true. \q He protects everyone who runs to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for safety.

decisions.reason: As silver is refined (Psalm 12:7), God's word has been tested and found true (Proverbs 30:5).
The word used of David in verse 24 is used of God's way.
With the article the word points to the God the song has been describing.
Psalm 18:31 has the same words.

source.text: כִּ֥י מִי־אֵ֖ל מִבַּלְעֲדֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וּמִ֥י צ֖וּר מִֽבַּלְעֲדֵ֥י אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For who [is] God except YHWH? And who [is] a rock except our God?

en.L: For who [is] God except {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? \q And who [is] a rock except our God?
en.B: Is there any God but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? \q Is there any rock but our God?
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is the only God. \q Only our God is strong and safe like a rock.

decisions.choice: who is God except the LORD?: there is none
decisions.reason: The questions expect the answer "no one" (Isaiah 44:8).
Psalm 18:32 has 'Eloah, a poetic form of the word for God, where this verse has 'El, and a different word for "except" (zulati) in the second line. The sense is the same.
Readable turns the questions into what they mean (m1), as at Psalm 18:32.

source.text: הָאֵ֥ל מָעוּזִּ֖י חָ֑יִל וַיַּתֵּ֥ר תָּמִ֖ים דַּרְכִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: The God [is] my refuge of strength, and he has set free blameless my way,

en.L: The God [is] my strong refuge, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has set my way free [and] blameless,
en.B: the God who is my strong fortress, \q who sets my way free and makes it secure,
en.R: God is my strong fortress. \q He clears my way and keeps me safe wherever I go.

decisions.reason: The word (ma'oz) is a stronghold, a safe place to flee to (Psalm 27:1; 31:5).

alternatives: has made my way blameless (as Psalm 18:33)
has set the blameless free on his way
decisions.reason: The verb (natar) means to loosen or set free. God clears David's way of what would hold him back, and keeps it whole (tamim), a road with no stumbling.

decisions.choice: my way: the word as read, not as written
alternatives: he sets the blameless free on his way (as written)
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text read "his way", and the form marked to be read aloud is "my way", as in Psalm 18:33. The words follow the form to be read.

Psalm 18:33 has "the God who girds me with strength and has made (yitten) my way blameless". Here God is "my strong refuge" (ma'uzzi in place of ha-me'azzereni), and the verb is "set free" (yatter), which differs by one letter.
The description of God continues through verse 35, so this verse ends with a comma.
Balanced gives the sense of "blameless" for a road, as at Psalm 18:33 (m2).

source.text: מְשַׁוֶּ֥ה רַגְלַ֖י כָּאַיָּל֑וֹת וְעַ֥ל בָּמוֹתַ֖י יַעֲמִדֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: making my feet like the does, and on my heights he makes me stand,

en.L: making my feet like the does', \q and on my heights {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes me stand,
en.B: who makes my feet as sure as a deer's \q and sets me firm on the heights,
en.R: He makes me sure-footed like a deer. \q He lets me stand safely high up in the mountains.

decisions.choice: like the does: sure-footed on the rocks
decisions.reason: Deer move swiftly and safely on steep crags (Habakkuk 3:19).
To stand on the heights is to hold the high ground, safe and in command (Deuteronomy 32:13).

decisions.choice: my feet: the word as read, not as written
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text read "his feet", and the form marked to be read aloud is "my feet", as in Psalm 18:34. The words follow the form to be read.
Psalm 18:34 has the same words, with a small difference of spelling in the last verb.

source.text: מְלַמֵּ֥ד יָדַ֖י לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וְנִחַ֥ת קֶֽשֶׁת־נְחוּשָׁ֖ה זְרֹעֹתָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: training my hands for the battle, and bends a bow of bronze my arms.

en.L: training my hands for battle, \q so that my arms bend a bow of bronze.
en.B: who trains my hands for war, \q so that my arms can draw a bronze bow.
en.R: He trains me to fight in battle. \q He makes my arms strong enough to bend a bow made of bronze.

decisions.choice: a bow of bronze: a bow only the strongest can bend
decisions.reason: Bows were made of wood and horn; a bow of bronze, or one fitted with bronze, would need great strength to draw (Job 20:24).
The description of God that began in verse 33 ends here.
Psalm 18:35 has the same words, with "bends" in a slightly different form.

source.text: וַתִּתֶּן־לִ֖י מָגֵ֣ן יִשְׁעֶ֑ךָ וַעֲנֹתְךָ֖ תַּרְבֵּֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And you have given me [the] shield of your salvation, and your answering makes me great.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given me the shield of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} answering has made me great.
en.B: You have handed me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} saving shield, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} answer has made me great.
en.R: You protect me and save me. \q You answer me, and that has made me great.

decisions.choice: the shield of your salvation: your protection that saves
decisions.reason: The shield is the salvation God gives.

decisions.choice: your answering: God answering my call
decisions.reason: The word ('anotkha) is most simply read as God's answer to David's call (verses 4 and 7). It can also be read, from a related root, as "your stooping down", God's humility in bending down to help, the word of Psalm 18:36.
Psalm 18:36 has a middle line, "and your right hand supports me", which this verse does not have, and "your humility" ('anvatkha) where this verse has "your answering" ('anotkha).

source.text: תַּרְחִ֥יב צַעֲדִ֖י תַּחְתֵּ֑נִי וְלֹ֥א מָעֲד֖וּ קַרְסֻלָּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: You make wide my steps under me, and not have slipped my ankles.

en.L: You make my steps wide under me, \q and my ankles have not slipped.
en.B: You make room for my steps, \q so my ankles do not turn.
en.R: You give me a wide, clear path, \q so I do not trip and fall.

decisions.choice: make wide my steps: give me room to walk safely
decisions.reason: As in verse 20, room is safety; a wide path has no traps.

decisions.choice: ankles: what gives way in a fall
decisions.reason: The word (qarsol) is found only here and in Psalm 18:37.
Psalm 18:37 has the same words, with "under me" written in a longer form.

source.text: אֶרְדְּפָ֥ה אֹיְבַ֖י וָאַשְׁמִידֵ֑ם וְלֹ֥א אָשׁ֖וּב עַד־כַּלּוֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: I pursued my enemies and destroyed them, and not did I turn back until they were finished.

en.L: I pursued my enemies and destroyed them, \q and I did not turn back until they were finished.
en.B: I chased my enemies and wiped them out; \q I did not give up the chase until I had made an end of them.
en.R: I chased my enemies and destroyed them. \q I did not stop until they were all gone.

decisions.choice: I pursued my enemies: victory as God's gift
decisions.reason: David's victories are told as the work of the God who trains and arms him (verses 33-36, 40).
Psalm 18:38 has "and overtook them" (assigem) where this verse has "and destroyed them" (ashmidem). The first verb is written here in a longer form (erdefah), with the same sense.

source.text: וָאֲכַלֵּ֥ם וָאֶמְחָצֵ֖ם וְלֹ֣א יְקוּמ֑וּן וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ תַּ֥חַת רַגְלָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I finished them and smashed them, and not did they rise; and they fell under my feet.

en.L: And I finished them and smashed them, and they did not rise; \q and they fell under my feet.
en.B: I made an end of them and shattered them, and they did not stand again; \q they lay fallen at my feet.
en.R: I wiped them out. I beat them so badly that they did not get up again. \q They fell down at my feet.

decisions.reason: A conquered enemy lay under the victor's feet (Psalm 110:1; Joshua 10:24).

decisions.choice: I finished them: the word of verse 38
decisions.reason: "I finished them" (kalah) takes up "until they were finished" at the end of verse 38.

Psalm 18:39 has "I smashed them, and they were not able to rise; they fell under my feet". This verse adds "I finished them" at the start, has "they did not rise" without "were able", and "and they fell" with "and".

source.text: וַתַּזְרֵ֥נִי חַ֖יִל לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה תַּכְרִ֥יעַ קָמַ֖י תַּחְתֵּֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And you girded me [with] strength for the battle; you made bow down those who rose against me under me.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} girded me [with] strength for battle; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made those who rose against me bow down under me.
en.B: You strapped strength on me for the fight; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought my attackers to their knees beneath me.
en.R: You made me strong for battle. \q You made my enemies fall down in front of me.

decisions.choice: girded me with strength: gave me strength
decisions.reason: A soldier tied his belt tight before battle; God fastens strength on David like a belt (1 Samuel 2:4).

decisions.choice: made bow down: brought to their knees
decisions.reason: The verb (kara') means to kneel or sink down, here in defeat.
Psalm 18:40 has the same words, with "you girded me" and "under me" written in slightly different forms.

source.text: וְאֹ֣יְבַ֔י תַּ֥תָּה לִּ֖י עֹ֑רֶף מְשַׂנְאַ֖י וָאַצְמִיתֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And my enemies you gave to me [the] neck; those who hated me, and I destroyed them.

en.L: And my enemies {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave to me [their] neck; \q those who hated me, I destroyed them.
en.B: You put my enemies to flight before me, \q and I destroyed those who hated me.
en.R: You made my enemies run away from me. \q I destroyed the people who hated me.

decisions.choice: you gave me the neck of my enemies: you made them flee
decisions.reason: To give someone the neck of an enemy is to make the enemy turn and run, showing the back of the neck (Exodus 23:27). It may also picture the victor's foot on the neck of the defeated.
Psalm 18:41 has "and those who hated me, I destroyed them"; here the "and" stands before "I destroyed them", and "you gave" is written in a shorter form. The sense is the same.

source.text: יִשְׁע֖וּ וְאֵ֣ין מֹשִׁ֑יעַ אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א עָנָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: They looked, but there was no one to save; to YHWH, but not did he answer them.

en.L: They looked, but there was no one to save; \q [they looked] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not answer them.
en.B: They looked for help, but no one came to save them; \q they looked to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them no answer.
en.R: They looked for help, but no one saved them. \q They even looked to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them no answer.

decisions.choice: he did not answer them: no help against God's king
decisions.reason: Those who fought the king the LORD had chosen found no help from him, as Saul, when he turned from God, received no answer (1 Samuel 28:6).

decisions.choice: they looked: they looked for help
decisions.reason: The verb (sha'ah) means to look to someone in hope of help (Isaiah 17:7-8).
The word for "savior" (moshia') is the one David uses of God in verse 3.
Psalm 18:42 has "they cried for help" (shava') where this verse has "they looked" (sha'ah), and another word for "to".
Balanced and Readable say what they looked for (m2).

source.text: וְאֶשְׁחָקֵ֖ם כַּעֲפַר־אָ֑רֶץ כְּטִיט־חוּצ֥וֹת אֲדִקֵּ֖ם אֶרְקָעֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I beat them fine like [the] dust of [the] earth; like [the] mud of [the] streets I crushed them, I stamped them down.

en.L: And I beat them fine like the dust of the earth; \q like the mud of the streets I crushed them, I stamped them down.
en.B: I ground them as fine as the dust of the ground; \q I crushed them and trampled them like mud in the streets.
en.R: I crushed them into dust. \q I stamped on them like mud in the street.

decisions.choice: I stamped them down: beat flat
decisions.reason: The verb (raqa') means to stamp with the feet or to beat flat (Ezekiel 25:6).

Psalm 18:43 has "like dust before the wind" where this verse has "like the dust of the earth", and one verb, "I emptied them out" (ariqem), where this verse has two, "I crushed them, I stamped them down" (adiqqem, erqa'em).

source.text: וַֽתְּפַלְּטֵ֔נִי מֵרִיבֵ֖י עַמִּ֑י תִּשְׁמְרֵ֨נִי֙ לְרֹ֣אשׁ גּוֹיִ֔ם עַ֥ם לֹא־יָדַ֖עְתִּי יַעַבְדֻֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And you delivered me from [the] strifes of my people; you kept me as head of nations; a people I did not know serve me.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} delivered me from the strifes of my people; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} kept me as the head of nations; \q a people I did not know serve me.
en.B: You set me free from the quarrels of my own people; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} kept me at the head of the nations. \q A nation I never knew now serves me.
en.R: You saved me when my own people fought against me. \q You kept me as ruler over other nations. People I did not even know now serve me.

decisions.choice: the strifes of my people: conflict at home
decisions.reason: The strife is within Israel: the war with Saul's house (chapters 2-4) and the revolts of Absalom and Sheba (chapters 15-20).

decisions.choice: head of nations: ruler over other peoples
decisions.reason: David's kingdom came to include Edom, Moab, Ammon and Aram (chapter 8).
Psalm 18:44 has "the people" where this verse has "my people", and "you made me" (tesimeni) where this verse has "you kept me" (tishmereni).

source.text: בְּנֵ֥י נֵכָ֖ר יִתְכַּֽחֲשׁוּ־לִ֑י לִשְׁמ֥וֹעַ אֹ֖זֶן יִשָּׁ֥מְעוּ לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Sons of foreignness cringe to me; at [the] hearing of [the] ear they obey me.

en.L: Sons of foreign lands cringe before me; \q at the hearing of the ear they obey me.
en.B: Foreigners come to me cringing; \q the moment they hear, they obey me.
en.R: People from other lands bow before me, afraid. \q The moment they hear about me, they obey me.

decisions.choice: cringe: give false or forced submission
decisions.reason: The verb (kachash) means to deceive or deny; here it is the forced, insincere humility of the defeated (Psalm 66:3; Deuteronomy 33:29).
"Sons of" names a group by what it belongs to.
Psalm 18:45 has the two lines in the other order, and slightly different forms of "cringe" and "hearing". The sense is the same.

source.text: בְּנֵ֥י נֵכָ֖ר יִבֹּ֑לוּ וְיַחְגְּר֖וּ מִמִּסְגְּרוֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Sons of foreignness wither, and they gird themselves from their strongholds.

en.L: Sons of foreign lands wither, \q and they gird themselves [to come] out of their strongholds.
en.B: Foreigners lose heart; \q they put on their belts and come out of their fortresses.
en.R: They lose their courage. \q They get ready and come out of their hiding places to give up.

decisions.choice: they gird themselves: they get ready to come out
decisions.reason: The verb (chagar) normally means to tie on a belt, to get ready to go out. Here the defeated foreigners make ready and leave their strongholds to surrender. Others take it as a rare word meaning "limp", or read the verb of Psalm 18:46, "they come trembling".
Like a plant drying up, their courage fails (Exodus 18:18 uses the same verb).
Psalm 18:46 has "they come trembling" (yachregu) where this verse has "they gird themselves" (yachgeru), the same letters in another order.
Readable says why they come out (m1).

source.text: חַי־יְהוָ֖ה וּבָר֣וּךְ צוּרִ֑י וְיָרֻ֕ם אֱלֹהֵ֖י צ֥וּר יִשְׁעִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Living [is] YHWH, and blessed [be] my rock, and may be exalted [the] God of [the] rock of my salvation,

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} lives! And blessed [be] my rock, \q and may the God of the rock of my salvation be exalted,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is alive! Blessed be my rock! \q May God, the rock who saves me, be lifted high,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is alive! Praise God, who is my rock! \q Praise God, the rock who saves me!

decisions.choice: The LORD lives: the living God
decisions.reason: The words are used in oaths ("as the LORD lives", 1 Samuel 14:39); here they are a shout of praise. The LORD, unlike idols, is alive and acts (Jeremiah 10:10).
To bless God is to praise him and speak well of him (Psalm 16:7).
The praise continues through verse 49, so this verse ends with a comma.
Psalm 18:47 has "the God of my salvation"; this verse has "the God of the rock of my salvation", taking up "rock" from the line before (compare verse 3).

source.text: הָאֵ֕ל הַנֹּתֵ֥ן נְקָמֹ֖ת לִ֑י וּמוֹרִ֥יד עַמִּ֖ים תַּחְתֵּֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: the God who gives vengeances for me, and bringing down peoples under me,

en.L: the God who gives vengeance for me \q and brings down peoples under me,
en.B: the God who avenges me \q and brings nations down beneath me,
en.R: God punishes my enemies for me. \q He brings nations down under my rule.

decisions.reason: Vengeance (neqamah) belongs to God (Deuteronomy 32:35). David does not take it for himself; God gives it, setting right the wrong done to him.
Psalm 18:48 has "and has subdued (yadber) peoples under me" where this verse has "and brings down (morid) peoples under me".

source.text: וּמוֹצִיאִ֖י מֵאֹֽיְבָ֑י וּמִקָּמַי֙ תְּר֣וֹמְמֵ֔נִי מֵאִ֥ישׁ חֲמָסִ֖ים תַּצִּילֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: and bringing me out from my enemies, and above those who rise against me you exalt me; from a man of violences you rescue me.

en.L: and who brings me out from my enemies; \q and above those who rise against me {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} exalt me; \q from a man of violence {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rescue me.
en.B: who brings me out from among my enemies. \q You raise me high above my attackers; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} save me from the violent man.
en.R: He brings me safely away from my enemies. \q You lift me high above people who attack me. You save me from the violent man.

decisions.choice: a man of violence: perhaps Saul
decisions.reason: The singular may point to one enemy, Saul (verse 1), or stand for every violent enemy (Psalm 140:2, 5). The plural "violences" means violence upon violence.
As in verse 29, the song turns from speaking of God to speaking to him.

Psalm 18:49 has "delivering me" (mefalleti) where this verse has "bringing me out" (motsi'i), "indeed above" where this verse has "and above", and "a man of violence" where this verse has the plural "violences".

source.text: עַל־כֵּ֛ן אוֹדְךָ֥ יְהוָ֖ה בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם וּלְשִׁמְךָ֖ אֲזַמֵּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore I will thank you, YHWH, among [the] nations, and to your name I will sing praises.

en.L: Therefore I will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, among the nations, \q and to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name I will sing praises.
en.B: That is why I will give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} thanks, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, among the nations, \q and sing praise to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.
en.R: So, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in front of people from every nation. \q I will sing praises to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: among the nations: quoted in Romans 15:9
decisions.reason: Paul quotes this line to show that Scripture foresaw people of every nation praising God through Christ (Romans 15:9).

decisions.choice: your name: God himself as he has made himself known
decisions.reason: The name stands for the person, and for all God has shown himself to be (Exodus 3:13-15).
Psalm 18:50 has "among the nations" before "LORD", and "I will sing praises" in a slightly longer form. The sense is the same.
Readable says "you" for "your name" (m2), as at Psalm 18:50.

source.text: מִגְדּ֖וֹל יְשׁוּע֣וֹת מַלְכּ֑וֹ וְעֹֽשֶׂה־חֶ֧סֶד לִמְשִׁיח֛וֹ לְדָוִ֥ד וּלְזַרְע֖וֹ עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: [A] tower of salvations [to] his king, and doing loyal love to his anointed, to David and to his offspring forever.

en.L: [He is] a tower of salvations [for] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} king, \q and showing loyal love to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anointed, to David and to his offspring forever."
en.B: He is a tower of victories for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} king; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keeps faith in loyal love with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anointed one, with David and his line for all time."
en.R: He is like a strong tower that gives {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} king great victories. \q He always shows faithful love to the king {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose, David, and to his children and grandchildren forever."

decisions.choice: a tower: the word as read, not as written
alternatives: making great the victories of his king (as written, and as Psalm 18:51)
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text read "making great" (magdil), as in Psalm 18:51, and the form marked to be read aloud is "tower" (migdol). The words follow the form to be read: God is a strong tower for his king (Proverbs 18:10).
The plural of yeshu'ah, salvation, here means acts of rescue, victories in battle (8:6, 14).

decisions.choice: his anointed, David and his offspring forever: the promise to David
decisions.reason: The king anointed by God (1 Samuel 16:13) is David, and the song ends with God's promise of a lasting line (7:12-16). "Anointed" (mashiach) is the word behind "Messiah" and "Christ", and the promise was later understood to point to the Messiah.

decisions.choice: loyal love: the faithful love God promised David
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is love that keeps its commitments. God promised that his chesed would not depart from David's son (7:15).
Psalm 18:51 reads "making great" (magdil) where this verse reads "tower" (migdol) (m1). The rest of the verse is the same.

This song is Psalm 18, and its wording is kept the same as the psalm wherever the Hebrew is the same. Psalm 18:51 has "loyal love" at Literal and Balanced and "faithful love" at Readable, so this verse does too, although elsewhere in 2 Samuel chesed is "steadfast love" at Literal and "faithful love" at Balanced (7:15).
Readable says what anointing meant: choosing someone as king.
